title: P22 — S3 file store
objective: Configurable per-environment buckets (DEF-015) across ALL FOUR hardcoded sites — the three recording handlers plus Topics/AttachFileToTopic, which the defect text missed; region-aware Minio client (Minio:Region on both the internal and the presign client); denied-create tolerance in EnsureBucketAsync (cloud IAM grants no s3:CreateBucket); CSP media-src matching the actual presign host; tests holding the >=95% per-file coverage gate. TWO DEVIATIONS from the intake text, both deliberate: (1) the nginx /acmp-recordings/ proxy is NEUTRALIZED, not deleted — its upstream moved to a variable + resolver so nginx no longer resolves 'minio' at config load and the cloud web container boots without it, while the on-prem/ngrok dev path (MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT = app host) keeps working; outright deletion would have regressed dev playback and forced a second nginx template ahead of P25. (2) the U1 spike splits: its offline half — endpoint rewriting, presign host, SigV4 region scope — is now PINNED BY TEST (MinioFileStoreCloudTests) and found that Minio 6.0.3 rewrites any Amazon host via AWSS3Endpoints to s3.amazonaws.com path-style for us-east-1, so the CSP origin is NOT ACMP_S3_ENDPOINT; its live half (real bucket, real multipart, browser playback) is not duplicated in a bespoke harness — it IS the AC-078 operator verification. The AWSSDK.S3 fallback was not built: nothing observed requires it.

title: P23 — Backup / restore / DR
objective: Drop WITH COMPRESSION (fails on Express); back up BOTH SQL databases (Acmp + keycloak); delete the pg_dump and mc-mirror legs; rewrite restore.sh (its psql-into-keycloak-db leg targeted a deleted container); aws s3 cp backups to the backup bucket; rollback + DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK-unwedge runbook. Verifies NFR-056/057/058. DELIVERED, plus four things the intake did not anticipate: (1) DEF-017 — the /backups mount is root-owned 0755 while SQL Server writes the .bak as uid 10001, so every backup would have failed silently; backup.sh now preflights it. (2) The S3 upload is NOT best-effort: a backup that exists only on the box being backed up is not a backup, so a failed upload fails the run. (3) restore.sh resolves every .bak BEFORE touching any database and stops only the dependents that are actually running, because a half-restored pair (new Acmp, stale keycloak) is worse than not starting. (4) 02-s3.sh now expires CURRENT versions on the backups bucket only — uncompressed nightly .bak files for two databases would otherwise accumulate forever on an account whose budget actions cut access at 100%. Local half of AC-080 is proved unattended by the new U4 gate (3 -> 0 -> 3 on keycloak, Express, no COMPRESSION, Keycloak healthy afterwards); the S3 leg and the Acmp database still need a live environment.

title: DW-029 batch 1: evidence three requirements that were built but never verifiable
objective: Start the DW-029 acceptance-criterion programme with a batch small enough to do impeccably, establishing the method the remaining batches follow. THE METHOD, stated once here: pick requirements that are ALREADY BUILT, write an acceptance criterion, and record a Met verdict with real evidence IN THE SAME BATCH - never leaving a Pending AC behind. That ordering is not stylistic. acs-met counts by retired_in and IGNORES lifecycle_status, so an AC written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false until that evidence exists; a bulk pass over all 135 would therefore make the package permanently un-ready, which is why DW-029 says it must not be run as one. THE SECOND RULE: verify the WHOLE criterion, not the part that is convenient. Both NFRs in this batch carry a 'Target:' clause stronger than the tests that existed - NFR-020's '0 unauthenticated non-health endpoints' was covered by three spot checks, and FR-151's eight named fields were covered by seven assertions. Where the evidence fell short of the requirement, the batch BUILT THE MISSING CONTROL rather than writing an AC around what happened to be tested.
